newsitem.title: UK: British Steel active in tax-related trade.
newsitem.headline: British Steel active in tax-related trade.

text.p: British Steel Plc was the most actively traded blue chip UK stock on Friday, after a tax-related "bed and breakfast" trade and as sterling strength continued to weigh on its profits outlook, traders said.
The stock failed to respond to strength elsewhere in the UK market and by 1033 GMT was down 1-3/4p at 162-1/2 in volume of 10.9 million shares.
The decline left the stock near its year's closing low of 159-1/2p set December 6.

Traders said volume was boosted by a bed-and-breakfast trade of 10 million shares, where an investor sells a poorly- performing stock to realise a loss for tax purposes and repurchases it the following day.
And they said U.S. buying of the company's ADRs last week had died out, removing another prop for the stock.

They said British Steel continued to be squeezed as a rising pound puts pressure on its earnings prospects for 1997. And they said some investors may be tempted to clear out a stock which has underperformed in recent months.

"People are probably getting rid of the skeletons in their closets," said one. "When you are British Steel you've only got to see the currency going against you for a length of time, and all of a sudden your margins get slammed."
